## Natural history notes

A small fruticose lichen characterized by gray-green basal scales and short, gritty-looking upright stalks tipped with bright red fruiting structures, giving it the classic “British soldiers” appearance. In Florida, it is found on exposed acidic soil, sandy ground, humus, rotting wood, and logs in open pinewoods, disturbed sandy areas, and other nutrient-poor habitats with enough light and moisture. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, helping colonize harsh surfaces while absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air rather than feeding on plants or wood directly.
